subject: octopus
pitch: A curious reef octopus in coral and rust tones, covered in little bumps and paler mottling. A soft, bulbous head, golden eyes with bar-shaped pupils and a slightly grumpy brow. Its eight arms curl out in every direction, each lined with rows of cream suckers, and one arm proudly holds up an old brass key it found on a shipwreck.

I'm planning a TypeScript module using the SDK to build an octopus model: a bulbous mantle, spherical eyes with pupils, and eight curved arms extending outward from the base.

For the arms, I'll chain curved catmull paths and sweep tapered tubes along them with coral/paint coloring, then add suckers as small cylinders placed along the underside of each arm using the sweep's normal frame. I'm also sketching a brass key held in one arm, mottled rust/coral tones via paint helpers, and small bump spheres for texture.

For eyes, I'm placing a golden sphere with a horizontal pupil bar on the mantle's surface, scattering sucker-like bumps across the body with a surface scatter function. I'm working out the overall rig: a root "body" joint with the mantle built as a lofted sweep along a vertical path, sizing the creature at roughly 0.6m span with a 0.22m mantle and 0.5m arms, set in a +Y up, +Z forward coordinate system.

Now I'm reconsidering the mantle shape, comparing a loft with explicit stations (including a bulbous head bulge partway up) against using a lathe to create a solid of revolution for a rounder, bulbous head. I'm sketching a profile outline for the lathe approach and weighing whether to stretch it along z afterward since lathe itself can't scale asymmetrically, ultimately leaning toward keeping the lathe symmetric and simple for the main head shape.

Now I'm planning the arms: eight tentacles radiating from the base using catmull-rom paths generated from a radial/height/curl function per arm, so each one spirals outward, downward, and curls at the tip, with small random variation for natural asymmetry.

I'll convert each arm path into a chain of auto-named joints parented to the body, using a naming function to keep segment names valid and unique. Then I'm building a tapered sweep mesh over each chain, with the radius function shrinking toward the tip for a natural tentacle shape.

For texture, I'm applying mottled rust-and-cream paint to the arms, then placing cylinder sucker geometry along the ventral side of each sweep using angle offsets to find belly-facing points, embedding them slightly into the surface.

I'm scaling back the sucker count to around 10 per row in two rows per arm to keep total mesh count reasonable, sharing a single geometry instance across all sucker meshes since three.js handles that fine for performance.

Now I'm planning scattered bumps on the mantle surface using small sphere geometries in a darker rust tone, and figuring out eye placement using surface hit queries around a center point with azimuth angles to position golden spheres symmetrically on either side of the mantle.

For the brow bar sitting on the surface, I should use the stick helper's spin option, which rotates about the normal axis directly rather than fighting with local Z rotations — I'll just pick a sign for left/right and accept some ambiguity there.
